report.clinical_summary: A 50-year-old man with a few years of diagnosis with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) in early stage, managed with 'watch and wait' - regular check-ups and blood tests, no active treatment. He presents with a small, tender lump in his neck that his wife noticed 2 weeks ago, and fatigue that feels different from his usual post-work tiredness - more of an overall sluggishness lasting throughout the day. He's been monitoring the lump himself and has been coming for regular check-ups. He understands his condition well and is actively engaged in managing his health.

The fatigue I've been experiencing lately feels somewhat different from my usual post-work tiredness. It's more of an overall feeling of sluggishness that lasts throughout the day

consequences.reasoning: The patient describes minimal impact on daily life overall, with only occasional fatigue being the most noticeable change. He's still managing his usual roles and activities, just being more aware of his energy levels.
